confirmed.title: Keystrokes typed during an in-flight save are silently lost: success path force-clears isDirty AND deletes the only durable IDB copy (R6 rationale is wrong)
confirmed.description: Failure scenario: (t0) writer is dirty, buffer tick writes draft D1 with words W1; (t1) autosave dispatches PUT(W1) — `md` is serialized at dispatch (manuscript-editor.tsx:501); (t2) writer types more words W2 during the PUT flight — `markDirty()` keeps isDirty true; (t2.5) a buffer tick writes draft D2 = W1+W2 and updates `lastBufferedHashRef`; (t3) PUT lands → success path runs `setLastSaved(new Date())` (line 526) which force-sets `isDirty: false` (editor-store.ts:126-127, `set({ lastSaved, isDirty: false, isSaving: false })`) and then `clearDraft(dispatchedChapterId)` (lines 530-532) deletes D2 — which contains W2, words the server does NOT have. Now: editor holds W1+W2, server holds W1, IDB holds nothing, isDirty is false. The code comment in use-draft-buffer.ts:199-202 claims "the next 2s tick recreates it" — this is FALSE: the buffer interval is gated on `isDirty` (use-draft-buffer.ts:218) and was just torn down, `bufferNow` itself early-returns on `!state.isDirty` (use-draft-buffer.ts:191), so even the pagehide/visibilitychange unload flush writes nothing, and the beforeunload prompt (manuscript-editor.tsx:692) doesn't fire because isDirty is false. The status bar shows "Saved HH:MM". If the writer stops typing (e.g. finished their last sentence mid-flight) and closes the tab, W2 is unrecoverable. The isDirty-clobber root is pre-existing (`setLastSaved` always cleared dirty), but this diff adds the draft deletion and the incorrect self-heal rationale — the one feature built to make this loss impossible actively deletes the safety copy during the exact window it exists for. Window = full PUT round-trip, which on the flaky networks this feature targets can be seconds.
confirmed.suggestion: In saveContent's success path (and the 409 no-op-adopt branch at lines 551-559), compare current editor content against the dispatched `md` before clearing dirty: if `getMarkdownFromEditor(editor) !== md`, call `markDirty()` immediately after `setLastSaved(...)` (or change setLastSaved to not touch isDirty and call markClean conditionally). With dirty preserved, the buffer interval keeps running and the hash reset in `clearDraft` guarantees the next tick re-persists W1+W2; the next autosave then ships W2. Also fix the R6 comment in use-draft-buffer.ts.

confirmed.title: SaveConflictDialog purges the IDB draft unconditionally (no onlyIfMine), destroying another tab's offline draft — and the owning tab's hash-skip prevents it from ever being rewritten
confirmed.description: `clearConflictDraft` calls `void deleteDraft(chapterId)` with NO `onlyIfMine` option (save-conflict-dialog.tsx:77), unlike the save-success path which deliberately uses `deleteDraft(chapterId, { onlyIfMine: true })` (use-draft-buffer.ts:251) to enforce spec §4.2: "one tab's save success cannot destroy another tab's offline draft". The dialog resolution IS a save-success path and bypasses that invariant. Failure scenario: tabs A and B have the same chapter open, both dirty; an agent rewrite 409s both tabs into conflict-suspension (autosave suspended in both). Tab A's buffer ticks have written its post-conflict words into the shared `chapterId`-keyed row (last-writer-wins per spec R8). The user resolves the conflict in tab B ("Keep mine") → `clearConflictDraft` unconditionally deletes the row holding tab A's words. Tab A cannot heal itself: its `lastBufferedHashRef` still matches its content, so every 2s tick hits the skip at use-draft-buffer.ts:197 (`if (hash === lastBufferedHashRef.current) return;`) and never rewrites — the deletion is invisible to tab A. Tab A's words now exist only in its DOM with autosave suspended (its conflict is still pending) and the localStorage conflict draft is write-only (spec R4 — never read back). If tab A crashes or is closed via the prompt before the user resolves its conflict, the words are permanently lost. The justification comment ("a re-offer on next load would present already-settled words as recovered") only holds for THIS tab's draft; a foreign-clientId row is by definition NOT settled by this dialog. Same unconditional-delete pattern (lower risk, sub-second race) exists in checkRecovery's hygiene delete at use-draft-buffer.ts:267.
confirmed.suggestion: Change save-conflict-dialog.tsx:77 to `void deleteDraft(chapterId, { onlyIfMine: true })`. A this-tab row is purged as intended; a foreign row survives and is correctly re-offered (with CAS backstop) on that tab's next load. Separately consider making the hash-skip self-healing, e.g. verify row existence on a slow cadence or reset the hash when a conflict is set.

confirmed.title: Tab duplication copies sessionStorage, so two tabs share one clientId — onlyIfMine cannot protect the most common second-tab scenario
confirmed.description: `getClientId()` persists the per-tab id in sessionStorage (draft-store.ts:101-113) and the comment claims it is "never shared across tabs" (line 90). That is false for the most common way a writer gets two tabs on the same chapter: duplicating the tab (Chrome/Edge/Firefox copy sessionStorage into the duplicate). Both tabs then stamp drafts with the SAME clientId, so `deleteDraft(..., { onlyIfMine: true })` (draft-store.ts:202-207) treats the other tab's draft as its own. Failure scenario: duplicated tabs A and B on one chapter, both dirty during an outage; on reconnect B's autosave wins → success-path `clearDraft` (manuscript-editor.tsx:530-532) deletes the shared row even when it currently holds A's divergent words (clientId matches). A's subsequent save 409s into conflict-suspension (autosave stops), its buffer ticks skip via the lastBufferedHashRef check (use-draft-buffer.ts:197 — A still believes its content is on disk), so A's words exist only in its DOM; a crash before the user resolves A's conflict loses them. This defeats exactly the invariant onlyIfMine was built for (spec §4.2), via standard browser behavior rather than a race.
confirmed.suggestion: Make the in-memory component authoritative for tab identity: on module load, generate a fresh id and write it back to sessionStorage (detecting duplication is impossible, but e.g. combining the sessionStorage id with a per-`window` random nonce held only in module scope gives a unique id per tab while keeping reload stability best-effort). Alternatively store `{ id, lockedAt }` and treat clientId as advisory: never hard-rely on it for deletes of rows whose content hash differs from this tab's lastBufferedHash.

confirmed.title: Keystrokes typed during an in-flight save are left with no durable copy after save success — R6 acceptance rationale is factually wrong
confirmed.description: Interleaving: (1) T0: pane dirty, debounce fires saveContent, serializes md0, PUT dispatched (slow link — exactly the network this feature targets). (2) T0+0.5s: writer types more words; onUpdate -> markDirty (isDirty stays true). (3) T0+2s: buffer tick putDraft writes md1 = md0 + new words to IDB — the new words now have a durable copy. (4) T0+2.5s: PUT resolves; success path runs setDocumentVersion, setLastSaved — which unconditionally sets isDirty:false (editor-store.ts:126-127) — then clearDraft(dispatchedChapterId) (manuscript-editor.tsx:530), which nulls lastBufferedHashRef and deletes the IDB row holding md1 (deleteDraft tx is created after the tick's putDraft tx, so IDB ordering guarantees the row dies). End state: the during-save keystrokes exist ONLY in the editor; isDirty is false so the buffer interval is torn down (use-draft-buffer.ts:217-223), bufferNow early-returns on the pagehide/visibilitychange flush (use-draft-buffer.ts:191), no autosave is scheduled (debounce effect gates on isDirty, manuscript-editor.tsx:611), no beforeunload prompt fires (gates on isDirty, line 692), and the status bar shows 'Saved HH:MM'. If the writer stops typing on those words and closes the tab — the canonical 'typed a final sentence, saw Saved, closed the laptop' flow — the words are silently lost, violating the cardinal rule while the UI actively claims durability. The R6 comment (use-draft-buffer.ts:199-202) accepts this window on the claim that 'the next 2s tick recreates it' — that claim is false in precisely the case that matters: setLastSaved wipes isDirty, so there is no next tick unless the writer types again. The identical hole exists in the 409 no-op-adopt branch (manuscript-editor.tsx:553-558). The pre-existing autosave had the same dirty-flag wipe, but this change is the one claiming the platform is now incapable of silent loss, and its new clearDraft is what destroys the durable copy the buffer had just created.
confirmed.suggestion: In saveContent's success and no-op-adopt paths, compare the current editor content against the dispatched md before declaring clean: if getMarkdownFromEditor(editor) (or its hash) differs from md, call markDirty() after setLastSaved and skip clearDraft (or re-trigger bufferNow). Alternatively give the pane store an edit epoch incremented by markDirty; capture it at serialization and have setLastSaved only clear isDirty when the epoch is unchanged. Either fix also repairs the beforeunload and unload-flush gating for free.
